name: Planning application dataset
fact: Planning Data reports 100,627 planning applications from 6 providers; collector and newest data are dated 17 September 2025 and the dataset is MHCLG-created pending authoritative replacement.
gate: Do not treat this dataset as a live national application register; verify the exact LPA register and current case status.

name: Planning decision dataset
fact: The planning-decision dataset currently reports 0 records, 0 providers and no collection attempt; origin is MHCLG-created pending authoritative replacement.
gate: Zero platform records must not be interpreted as no planning decisions; use authoritative LPA/PINS decision sources.

name: Planning application status dataset
fact: The platform dataset has 0 collected records, while the data design model defines controlled planning-application status codes.
gate: Use the codes as schema semantics only; they do not prove any application's current status.

name: Planning application type dataset
fact: Planning Data exposes 41 planning-application types; collector last ran 17 September 2025 and origin is MHCLG-created pending authoritative replacement.
gate: Type classification is not application validity, decision or permission evidence.

name: Planning permission status dataset
fact: Three permission statuses are defined: permissioned, not-permissioned and pending-decision; collector last ran 23 July 2026.
gate: A status must be tied to the exact current site/application record and dates; category existence alone proves nothing.

name: Planning permission type dataset
fact: Seven permission types are defined, including full, outline, reserved matters, permission in principle and technical details consent.
gate: Permission type does not prove a permission remains live, implemented or complete.

name: Planning condition dataset
fact: Planning Data reports 5,605 planning conditions from one provider; collector last ran 20 July 2026 but origin is MHCLG-created pending authoritative replacement.
gate: Condition text must be linked to the exact permission and discharge/compliance state before affecting deliverability.

name: Planning condition type dataset
fact: The planning-condition-type dataset currently has 0 records and no collection attempt.
gate: No platform type record is not evidence that a permission has no conditions.

name: Article 4 direction dataset
fact: Planning Data reports 3,167 Article 4 directions from 101 providers; collector and newest data reached 21 July 2026, with some MHCLG-created data still present.
gate: Coverage is not nationally complete; exact live direction document and rule must be checked before parcel use.

name: Article 4 direction area dataset
fact: Planning Data reports 7,133 Article 4 direction areas from 110 providers; collector and newest data reached 22 July 2026.
gate: Area intersection only signals a possible permitted-development restriction; the exact direction/rule and effective dates remain required.

name: Brownfield land dataset
fact: Planning Data reports 37,666 brownfield-land records from 354 providers; collector last ran 20 July 2026 and newest data was found 16 July 2026; all data is from authoritative sources.
gate: Register inclusion is not planning permission, availability, title control or remaining capacity.

name: Brownfield site experimental boundary dataset
fact: The experimental brownfield-site dataset reports 2,916 site boundaries from 5 providers; collector last ran 23 July 2026 and origin is MHCLG-created pending authoritative replacement.
gate: Do not substitute experimental boundary coverage for the authoritative brownfield-land record or exact title geometry.

name: Planning application submissions design project
fact: MHCLG Digital Planning is developing open reusable specifications for planning-application submissions; the project page lists a community session on 22 July 2026.
gate: Design/specification work is not a live application or decision source.

name: Planning application submissions roadmap
fact: The 2026 roadmap describes work on mandating submission specifications and an initial planning-decision specification through March 2026.
gate: A roadmap milestone is not evidence that authoritative national decision data is already available.

name: Planning application status code finder
fact: The official data editor lists 10 planning-application status codes, including appeal granted/refused, decision appealed and expired.
gate: Schema status codes must not be assigned to a live case without authoritative case evidence.

name: Planning application type code finder
fact: The official data editor exposes 41 application-type codes for use in planning application data.
gate: Correct code use is schema validation, not permission or decision evidence.

name: Planning decision type code finder
fact: The official finder lists planning-officer, committee and secretary-of-state decision types.
gate: Decision-maker classification does not state the outcome of an application.

name: Planning decision type dataset design links
fact: The data editor links planning-decision-type to the planning applications decisions design work and platform/API schema.
gate: Design provenance is not a live decision record.

name: Planning application type schema
fact: The schema includes entity, reference, description, planning-application-category and date fields for application types.
gate: Schema structure does not determine a site's application state.

name: Planning application status change log
fact: The change log shows the expired status added 18 January 2024 and the other status records added 28 September 2023.
gate: Model change dates are not application-event dates.

name: Planning permission status history
fact: The history lists permissioned, not-permissioned and pending-decision records, each starting 4 February 2021.
gate: Controlled-status history is not evidence of any site's current permission state.

name: Planning appeals procedural guide after 1 April 2026
fact: Updated 16 July 2026; this guide applies to appeals relating to applications submitted on or after 1 April 2026 and covers refusal, conditions and non-determination routes.
gate: Use the exact application submission date before choosing the procedural route; an appeal right is not an appeal outcome.

name: Planning appeals procedural guide to 31 March 2026
fact: Updated 16 July 2026; this guide applies to appeals relating to applications dated on or before 31 March 2026.
gate: Do not apply the legacy route to post-31-March applications.

name: Planning Inspectorate appeals collection
fact: The Planning Inspectorate collection groups appeal types, search/comment services, costs and participation guidance; it was updated 16 April 2026.
gate: A route index is procedural context, not case status.

name: Appeals how long they take
fact: For cases decided in March 2026, s78 written-representation appeals had a 16-week median and 21-week mean; PINS warns recent-case averages should not predict a new case.
gate: Historic aggregate timescales must not be stored as a case-specific decision date.

name: Called-in planning applications procedural guide
fact: Updated 26 February 2026; the guide explains roles, timetable, procedure, evidence and publication of decisions for called-in applications.
gate: Called-in procedure is distinct from a normal LPA decision or s78 appeal.

name: Taking part in planning/listed-building/enforcement appeals
fact: The collection links 2026 written-representation, hearing, inquiry and Rule 6 participation guidance.
gate: Participation rights do not imply appeal validity or outcome.

name: Planning appeals written representations taking part
fact: Updated 18 May 2026 to reflect the new written representations Part 1 process.
gate: Interested-party participation is evidence input, not a decision.

name: Appeal or search for a planning decision or notice
fact: GOV.UK routes users to appeal planning decisions/notices and to search or comment on cases through the Appeals Casework Portal.
gate: Portal availability is not evidence that a specific appeal exists or has been decided.

name: Claim planning appeal costs overview
fact: The current costs service allows awards where unreasonable behaviour causes appeal-related costs; timing depends on procedure.
gate: A costs claim or award is separate from the merits/outcome of the planning appeal.

name: Claim planning appeal costs how to claim
fact: Costs may be claimed using the form or letter explaining unreasonable behaviour and resulting expense.
gate: Submitting a costs claim does not establish entitlement or appeal success.

name: Claim planning appeal costs when to claim
fact: The service sets procedure-specific deadlines and limits claims to costs directly related to the appeal.
gate: Costs deadlines are procedural and do not alter permission status.

name: S106 modification/discharge appeal guide
fact: The guide covers appeals where an LPA refuses or fails to determine an application to modify/discharge a planning obligation under S106.
gate: A S106B appeal concerns the obligation and does not itself grant underlying planning permission or site delivery.
